statement: Afonso I (r. 1509-1542), not João I, durably established Christianity as Kongo's state religion: he declared traditional "idol" worship illegal, burned at least one traditional shrine/temple, built churches/schools in the provinces, and used Christian doctrines of primogeniture/divine right to strengthen his own succession claim against rival lineage contenders. His surviving correspondence (John K. Thornton, Afonso I Mvemba a Nzinga, King of Kongo: His Life and Correspondence, Hackett, 2020, trans. Luís Madureira) includes a series beginning 1526 protesting the escalating, increasingly uncontrolled Atlantic slave trade to King João III of Portugal — even while Afonso himself operated a regulated slave trade.

sources.citation: Thornton, John K. Afonso I Mvemba a Nzinga, King of Kongo: His Life and Correspondence. Hackett Publishing, 2020.
sources.author: John K. Thornton

notes: The commonly cited "24 letters" figure applies specifically to the 1526+ anti-slave-trade series; the total surviving correspondence collected in Thornton's 2020 volume may be larger — not independently verified against the book's table of contents.
